summary_oneline: Reuse model execution plans; evaluate sequential Rust and selective bulk parallelism with behavioral parity.

constraints.statement: Complete backward compatibility required; deployed baseline not yet identified
Dynamic fields and metadata prevent naive permanent schema snapshots
Rust scalar implementations already differ from legacy numeric behavior
Parallel work must preserve callback and exception ordering

enrichment.scope: Differential baseline, loop-level validation gating using precomputed remaining work and proven conversion postconditions, class-owned execution plan, sequential Cython/Rust comparison, selective bulk parallelism and independent serialization experiment.

confidence_map.statement: Per-instance overhead remains despite existing caches
Local benchmark reproduces the reported order of slowdown
Rust integer substitution can break compatibility
Class-owned plans and coarse sequential execution are promising
Larger pure workloads are better parallel candidates
Specific speedup and full company compatibility remain unestablished
Validation dispatch is unconditional for fields reaching the validation stage; absent user options do not remove implicit checks
A conservative precomputed work mask and proven conversion postconditions can target unnecessary dispatch

unknowns.question: Which deployed version and company ORM corpus define compatibility?
Which workloads and performance targets have priority?

recommended_next_command.rationale: Baseline ownership and execution-boundary choices need discussion before a scoped specification.

meta.notes: Native internals unprofiled; no implementation or speedup claimed. User parallelism and loop-level gating suggestions included. The reported 220000 calls and approximately 15 microseconds are user-provided; safe removable work remains to be measured.
